items.instruction:
You ordered a washing machine from an online shop. It arrived two weeks late, and when it was installed you found that it was damaged.

Write a letter to the customer services manager of the shop. In your letter:
• give details of your order
• describe the problems with the delivery and the machine
• say what you would like the shop to do

Write at least 150 words. You do not need to include any addresses.
Begin your letter with: Dear Sir or Madam,

You would like to take an evening course at a local college, but the college website does not give all the information you need.

Write a letter to the college. In your letter:
• say which course you are interested in and why
• explain what experience you already have in this subject
• ask for the information you need

Write at least 150 words. You do not need to include any addresses.
Begin your letter with: Dear Sir or Madam,

For the last month, building work near your home has continued late into the evening and sometimes starts very early in the morning.

Write a letter to your local council. In your letter:
• describe the building work and when it happens
• explain how it is affecting you and other residents
• suggest what the council should do

Write at least 150 words. You do not need to include any addresses.
Begin your letter with: Dear Sir or Madam,

You have seen an advertisement for a part-time job as a weekend guide at a museum in your town.

Write a letter to the manager of the museum. In your letter:
• say where you saw the advertisement and why you are interested
• describe your relevant experience and skills
• explain when you would be available to work

Write at least 150 words. You do not need to include any addresses.
Begin your letter with: Dear Sir or Madam,

You recently travelled by train and left a bag on the train when you got off.

Write a letter to the lost property office of the train company. In your letter:
• give details of your journey
• describe the bag and what was in it
• say how the company can contact you and return it

Write at least 150 words. You do not need to include any addresses.
Begin your letter with: Dear Sir or Madam,

You often visit a park near your home, but you feel that it has not been well looked after recently.

Write a letter to the parks department of your city. In your letter:
• explain how often you use the park and what you use it for
• describe what is wrong with the park now
• suggest how it could be improved

Write at least 150 words. You do not need to include any addresses.
Begin your letter with: Dear Sir or Madam,

You stayed at a hotel for three nights last month. After you returned home, you noticed that the hotel had charged your card twice.

Write a letter to the manager of the hotel. In your letter:
• give details of your stay
• explain the problem with the payment
• say what you want the hotel to do

Write at least 150 words. You do not need to include any addresses.
Begin your letter with: Dear Sir or Madam,

You have read in a local newspaper that the town plans to close one of its public libraries to save money.

Write a letter to the editor of the newspaper. In your letter:
• explain why this library is important to you
• describe who else would be affected by the closure
• suggest another way for the town to save money

Write at least 150 words. You do not need to include any addresses.
Begin your letter with: Dear Sir or Madam,

You need to take a week off work next month for an important family event.

Write a letter to your manager. In your letter:
• explain why you need the time off
• say which days you would like to take
• suggest how your work could be done while you are away

Write at least 150 words. You do not need to include any addresses.
Begin your letter with: Dear …,

You rent a flat, and the heating has stopped working. You have already tried to contact your landlord by phone without success.

Write a letter to your landlord. In your letter:
• describe the problem with the heating
• explain how it is affecting you
• say when it would be convenient for someone to repair it

Write at least 150 words. You do not need to include any addresses.
Begin your letter with: Dear …,

Your neighbour's dog barks for most of the day while your neighbour is at work. You do not know this neighbour well.

Write a letter to your neighbour. In your letter:
• describe the problem
• explain why it is difficult for you
• suggest a solution

Write at least 150 words. You do not need to include any addresses.
Begin your letter with: Dear …,

You are taking an evening course, and you have missed the last two classes because you were ill.

Write a letter to your teacher. In your letter:
• explain why you missed the classes
• ask what you need to do to catch up
• say when you expect to return

Write at least 150 words. You do not need to include any addresses.
Begin your letter with: Dear …,

You are applying for a new job, and the employer has asked for a reference from someone who knows your work.

Write a letter to a former manager. In your letter:
• remind them who you are and when you worked together
• describe the job you are applying for
• explain why you are asking them for a reference

Write at least 150 words. You do not need to include any addresses.
Begin your letter with: Dear …,

You are a member of a local sports club, and the training sessions have recently been moved to a time that does not suit many members.

Write a letter to the organiser of the club. In your letter:
• say how long you have been a member
• explain the problem with the new training times
• suggest a better arrangement

Write at least 150 words. You do not need to include any addresses.
Begin your letter with: Dear …,

You have an idea that you think would make your workplace a better place to work.

Write a letter to your manager. In your letter:
• describe the current situation at work
• explain your idea
• say how staff and the company would benefit

Write at least 150 words. You do not need to include any addresses.
Begin your letter with: Dear …,

You recently stayed in a small guest house run by its owner. When you got home, you realised you had left something behind.

Write a letter to the owner of the guest house. In your letter:
• thank them for your stay
• describe what you left behind and where
• ask them to send it to you and offer to pay the cost

Write at least 150 words. You do not need to include any addresses.
Begin your letter with: Dear …,

You have recently moved to a new home in another town.

Write a letter to a friend. In your letter:
• describe your new home and the area
• invite your friend to visit
• suggest some things you could do together

Write at least 150 words. You do not need to include any addresses.
Begin your letter with: Dear …,

A friend invited you to their birthday party, but you were not able to go.

Write a letter to your friend. In your letter:
• apologise and explain why you could not come
• ask about the party
• suggest a time to meet and celebrate together

Write at least 150 words. You do not need to include any addresses.
Begin your letter with: Dear …,

A friend looked after your home and your pet while you were away on holiday.

Write a letter to your friend. In your letter:
• thank your friend for their help
• tell them about your holiday
• offer to do something for them in return

Write at least 150 words. You do not need to include any addresses.
Begin your letter with: Dear …,

A friend is going to study in the city where you live and has asked you for advice.

Write a letter to your friend. In your letter:
• give advice about where to live
• describe what you like about the city
• offer to help when they arrive

Write at least 150 words. You do not need to include any addresses.
Begin your letter with: Dear …,

You started a new job a month ago, and you have not had a chance to tell an old friend about it.

Write a letter to your friend. In your letter:
• describe your new job
• say what you like and dislike about it
• explain how your daily life has changed

Write at least 150 words. You do not need to include any addresses.
Begin your letter with: Dear …,

A friend lent you their camera for a trip, and it was damaged while you were using it.

Write a letter to your friend. In your letter:
• explain what happened to the camera
• apologise for the damage
• say what you will do to put things right

Write at least 150 words. You do not need to include any addresses.
Begin your letter with: Dear …,

You are organising a meeting of people who were in your class at school ten years ago.

Write a letter to a friend from your class. In your letter:
• give details of the event
• explain why you need help with the organisation
• suggest what your friend could do

Write at least 150 words. You do not need to include any addresses.
Begin your letter with: Dear …,

You recently went to the wedding of a friend you both know, but your friend could not come.

Write a letter to your friend. In your letter:
• describe the wedding
• say what you enjoyed most about the day
• give some news about other people who were there

Write at least 150 words. You do not need to include any addresses.
Begin your letter with: Dear …,
